title: Quasi-compact scheme immersions descend over faithfully flat affine bases
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $p:V\to U$ be a flat surjective morphism of affine $S$-schemes [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $f:X\to U$ be a morphism of schemes. If $X\times_UV\to V$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a quasi-compact immersion, then $f$ is a quasi-compact immersion. Immersion means a factorization as a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]; quasi-compact means that inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. No Noetherian or finite-presentation assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 02L8 (lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact-immersion), descent implication for the singleton fpqc covering by a flat surjective affine-to-affine map.

proof.text: Put $X'=X\times_UV$ and write $f':X'\to V$. Affine schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Consequently $p$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). The immersion $f'$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation](a). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-quasi-compact] and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-separated] to the given flat surjective $p$: $f$ is quasi-compact and separated.

source.place: Tag 02L8, lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact-immersion, proof; scheme-image base change expanded using the dense case of Tag 081I.

proof.text: Form $f=i\circ a$ with $a:X\to Z=\operatorname{SIm}(f)$ and $i:Z\hookrightarrow U$ using [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc]. This also gives injectivity of $\mathcal O_Z\to a_*\mathcal O_X$. The affine description of closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes $Z$ affine because $U$ is affine. The scheme $X$ is quasi-compact by step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2). Since $Z$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], part (1) of the same permanence node makes $a$ quasi-compact. It is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation](b), applied to $i\circ a=f$, and hence quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. The injectivity above and the kernel definition [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] say that $a$ has scheme-theoretic image $Z$.

source.place: Tag 02L8, lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact-immersion, proof; scheme-image base change expanded using the dense case of Tag 081I.

proof.text: Let $Z'=Z\times_UV$, with $i':Z'\to V$ and $q:Z'\to Z$. Base change of the closed immersion $i$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], so $Z'$ is affine by the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The map $q$ is flat and surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Fibre-product associativity [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $X\times_ZZ'$ with $X'$ and gives $f'=i'\circ b$, where $b:X'\to Z'$ is the base change of $a$. It is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Apply the dense-case statement of [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] to the quasi-compact quasi-separated $a$ and flat $q$: $b$ has scheme-theoretic image $Z'$. Since $b$ is quasi-compact, [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] identifies its kernel ideal with the actual sheaf kernel, so $\mathcal O_{Z'}\to b_*\mathcal O_{X'}$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 02L8, lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact-immersion, proof; scheme-image base change expanded using the dense case of Tag 081I.

proof.text:
For every affine open $W\subseteq V$, the factorization $f'=i'\circ b$ gives
$$\mathcal O_V(W)\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{Z'}((i')^{-1}W)\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{X'}((f')^{-1}W),$$
where the second arrow is injective by step 3. Thus the kernel of the composite equals that of the first arrow. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel](1), applied to quasi-compact $f'$, these are exactly the ideals on $W$ of $\operatorname{SIm}(f')$ and $Z'$. Equality on the affine basis identifies the closed subschemes over $V$, since by the affine description of closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] each is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the quotient by this ideal over every affine open $W$. Their factor maps agree, since a closed immersion is a monomorphism (the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel]). Therefore $b$ identifies with the canonical factor of $f'$ through its image. By [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image], this factor is an open immersion, since $f'$ is a quasi-compact immersion.

source.place: Tag 02L8, lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact-immersion, proof; scheme-image base change expanded using the dense case of Tag 081I.

proof.text: Apply [lem-galois-open-immersion-affine-descent] to $a:X\to Z$ and $q:Z'\to Z$. Both $Z$ and $Z'$ are affine (steps 2--3), $q$ is flat and surjective, and the second projection of the pullback of $a$ along $q$ is $b$, an open immersion by step 4. Thus $a$ is an open immersion. Both $a$ and the closed immersion $i$ are immersions by [def-weil-closed-immersion] (use the identity as the other factor); their composite $f=i\circ a$ is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). Step 1 already proved that $f$ is quasi-compact. This proves both requested properties without a Noetherian or finite-presentation hypothesis.
